business_problem: Zelma needed to make fragmented K-12 assessment data usable for parents, educators, and policymakers because the information was scattered across portals and formats and was too hard for most people to query or visualize.
solution_summary: Zelma turns public education data into a conversational analytics experience by combining a cleaned national dataset with GPT-4 and the OpenAI API. Brown University researchers first gathered and normalized standardized-test data into one format, then Novy used function calling to tell GPT-4 which charts, fields, and views to use when answering user questions. For the Ask a Question interface, Zelma fine-tuned a model to provide data-aware typeahead suggestions and embedded known-good example graphs in a vector database to improve accuracy on edge cases. Questions in plain language enter the interface, the OpenAI-backed orchestration layer maps them to relevant datasets and visuals, and Zelma returns charts, SQL logic, and plain-language context about caveats such as assessment changes. That design makes school-performance analysis faster, more transparent, and more accessible to nontechnical audiences.
